title: Git worktrees create linked working directories
claim: `git worktree add <path> <commit-ish>` creates a new working tree linked to the same repository while keeping per-worktree files such as HEAD and index separate.
evidence: Context7 `/git/htmldocs` git-worktree docs: worktree add creates a linked worktree and shares repository content except per-worktree files such as HEAD and index.
relevance: Supports running each Cartographer topic in its own checkout without cloning the repository for every topic.

title: Git worktrees support separate branches and listing
claim: Git worktree commands can add a worktree for a branch/path and `git worktree list` reports path, commit, branch, and state annotations such as locked or prunable.
evidence: Context7 `/git/htmldocs` git-worktree docs show `git worktree add <path> [<commit-ish>]` and `git worktree list` output with branch/state details.
relevance: Enables a Cartographer worktree status/preflight step that reports active topic worktrees and branch health.

title: Git avoids duplicate active branch checkouts
claim: When adding a worktree for a branch, Git treats an existing branch checked out elsewhere as a special case that normally requires force to override; practical workflows should use a unique branch per topic worktree.
evidence: Context7 `/git/htmldocs` git-worktree docs note an existing branch is checked out unless already in use elsewhere and `--force` can override certain checks.
relevance: Constrains the proposal to one branch per Cartographer topic and avoids running multiple topics against the same branch.

title: Brave Search result for official git-worktree documentation
Official Git docs describe multiple working trees
claim: The official git-scm documentation describes a repository as supporting multiple working trees, allowing more than one branch to be checked out at a time, with metadata differentiating linked worktrees.
evidence: Brave Search result for `Git - git-worktree Documentation`: a Git repository can support multiple working trees and `git worktree add` associates a new working tree with repository metadata.
relevance: Provides external validation that the requested parallel topic model is an intended Git use case.

title: Async subagents are not parallel writes by default
claim: pi-subagents guidance says async does not mean parallel writes; agents should not edit the same active worktree concurrently unless writers are isolated in separate worktrees.
evidence: The pi-subagents skill states parent-side overlap should be reading, validation prep, synthesis, command planning, or review unless the writer is isolated in a separate worktree.
relevance: Motivates Cartographer's explicit worktree mode instead of simply launching concurrent implementers against one checkout.

title: pi-subagents can isolate parallel tasks with worktrees
claim: pi-subagents supports `worktree: true` for parallel tasks, giving each task its own git worktree branched from HEAD, requiring a clean git state and targeting intentionally parallel write workflows.
evidence: The pi-subagents skill's Worktree Isolation section documents `worktree: true`, isolated worktrees branched from HEAD, and a clean-state requirement.
relevance: Shows a proven local orchestration primitive Cartographer can align with or document alongside topic-level worktrees.

title: Cartographer workflow has proposal-plan-implement stages
claim: Pi Cartographer turns a rough request into a proposal, an ordered implementation plan, and implementation with phase-by-phase code changes that must pass validation.
evidence: README.md describes the three outputs: proposal, ordered implementation plan, and phase-by-phase implementation with validation.
relevance: Defines the workflow that worktree mode must preserve rather than replace.

title: Cartographer topic artifacts are commit-worthy rationale
claim: Cartographer writes topic planning artifacts under `.plan/<topic>/`, and those topic artifacts are intentional rationale to review and commit when they explain the work.
evidence: README.md's What gets written section lists `.plan/<topic>/proposal.md`, plan/map/fact JSONL files, and says these topic artifacts are intentional rationale.
relevance: Constrains worktree branches to carry their own `.plan/<topic>` artifacts through merge, while keeping generated caches out of commits.

title: Implement skill already has git safety gates
claim: The implement skill checks `git status --short`, records the branch and commit SHA, avoids unrelated user changes, and creates conventional commits for completed phases.
evidence: skills/implement/SKILL.md documents preflight repository safety and phase completion/commit steps.
relevance: Worktree mode can extend existing safety gates instead of inventing an entirely new implementation path.

title: The shared index is generated and ignored
claim: The index-project skill stores the SQLite index and manifest under `.plan/_index/`, ensures `.plan/_index/` and `.plan/_private/` are ignored, and treats proposal/plan JSONL artifacts as topic source-of-truth files.
evidence: skills/index-project/SKILL.md describes `.plan/_index/` artifacts, ignore behavior, and topic map/proposal artifacts as source-of-truth planning files.
relevance: Each topic worktree should regenerate its own index cache and merge only topic rationale/source changes.

title: User wants concurrent feature topics
claim: The requested outcome is to run Cartographer workflows in git worktrees so multiple feature topics can be worked on and implemented at once before merging back to the main branch.
evidence: User requested a proposal for running the Cartographer workflow in git worktrees to allow multiple feature topics to be worked on and implemented at once before merging to main.
relevance: Primary scope driver for this proposal.
